lines: My team did an experiment to see how to make more people donate money.
We sent two types of messages to former students who did not want to donate.
One message said, “Your gift helps students and teachers.”
The other said, “Giving makes you feel happy.”
Each message worked well — about 6.5% of the students chose to donate.
Next, we put the two messages together, expecting it would work better.
Less than 3% gave money after reading both messages.
Each message alone worked twice as well as both together.
When we gave them two different reasons at the same time, they felt we were trying too hard to change their minds.
As a result, they didn’t trust us and decided not to donate.
If you push too much, people may not do what you want.
body.text: My team did an experiment to see how to make more people donate money. We sent two types of messages to former students who did not want to donate. One message said, “Your gift helps students and teachers.” The other said, “Giving makes you feel happy.” Each message worked well — about 6.5% of the students chose to donate. Next, we put the two messages together, expecting it would work better. But it didn’t. Less than 3% gave money after reading both messages. Each message alone worked twice as well as both together. Why did this happen? When we gave them two different reasons at the same time, they felt we were trying too hard to change their minds. As a result, they didn’t trust us and decided not to donate. If you push too much, people may not do what you want.
